content.introduction: The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) is a leading securities marketplace located in New York City, offering a platform for trading stocks, options, and exchange-traded products. It is the largest stock exchange in the world and the epicenter of capitalism in the US. The NYSE is also planning to launch an exchange in Texas, renaming NYSE Chicago to NYSE Texas to cater to companies looking for a home base in the business-friendly state. The NYSE is part of Intercontinental Exchange and was previously the Chicago Stock Exchange. SEC Chairman Paul Atkins rang the opening bell at the NYSE on December 2, 2025, and delivered a speech on revitalizing America's markets. The NYSE is located at 11 Wall St, New York, NY, 10005.

Trading at the NYSE exchanges and most major stock exchanges around the world is done almost entirely electronically. Stocks trade on multiple exchanges even if they have one designated as their primary listing. [...] In this article

The New York Stock Exchange will soon have a presence in Texas to cater to the growing number of companies looking for a home base in the business-friendly state.

The NYSE announced Wednesday that one of its electronic exchanges, NYSE Chicago, will reincorporate in Texas and be renamed NYSE Texas, giving companies an option to list their stocks in the Lone Star State. [...] "As the state with the largest number of NYSE listings, representing over $3.7 trillion in market value for our community, Texas is a market leader in fostering a pro-business atmosphere," Lynn Martin, president of NYSE Group, said in a release.

The NYSE is part of Intercontinental Exchange. NYSE Chicago was previously the Chicago Stock Exchange, which was acquired by ICE in 2018.

On the cusp of America's 250th anniversary, SEC Chairman Paul Atkins rang the opening bell at the New York Stock Exchange (9:15 a.m.) and delivered a major speech (10 a.m.) entitled “Revitalizing America's Markets at 250” to outline his vision to strengthen U.S. capital markets for the next century and what the SEC is doing now to lay that groundwork.
